pr.title: Fix `ByMove` coroutine-closure shim (for 2021 precise closure capturing behavior)
pr.description:
This PR reworks the way that we perform the `ByMove` coroutine-closure shim to account for the fact that the upvars of the outer coroutine-closure and the inner coroutine might not line up due to edition-2021 closure capture rules changes.

Specifically, the number of upvars may differ *and/or* the inner coroutine may have additional projections applied to an upvar. This PR reworks the information we pass into the `ByMoveBody` MIR visitor to account for both of these facts.

I tried to leave comments explaining exactly what everything is doing, but let me know if you have questions.

r? oli-obk
pr.author: compiler-errors

analysis.summary: The ByMoveBody shim in StateTransform incorrectly assumed a one-to-one, same-shape correspondence between an outer coroutine-closure's upvars and the inner coroutine's upvars. Edition-2021 precise captures can split one parent capture into multiple child captures, add projections, and renumber fields, so the old zip_eq-based remapping produced wrong places. The fix builds an explicit child→parent field remapping keyed by upvar base HIR id plus projection prefix, re-applies extra precise-capture projections, and tolerates implicit reborrow derefs.
analysis.originalLogic: The pass builds a by-move body for a coroutine-closure by remapping the inner coroutine's captured fields back onto the parent closure's by-value upvars. It skipped the call arguments, then paired the remaining child captures with parent captures using `.zip_eq(tcx.closure_captures(parent_def_id))`, collected a `by_ref_fields` set when `coroutine_capture.is_by_ref() && !parent_capture.is_by_ref()`, and asserted `coroutine_capture.place.ty() == parent_capture.place.ty()`. In the visitor, for a captured field it rebuilt the place as `Field(idx, peeled_ty)` followed by the remaining original projection, peeling one deref only for fields in `by_ref_fields`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical rewrite positionally zipped child and parent captures, effectively assuming the number and shape of upvars are identical. Under edition-2021 precise captures, one parent capture may correspond to several child captures; the child may have additional projections (fields/derefs) applied, and child field indices differ from parent field indices. The old code would therefore remap a child field to the wrong parent field, fail the type-equality assertion, or fail to re-apply the extra precise-capture projections. It also matched captures by projection kind alone (so two different upvars with identical projection shapes could be confused) and assumed exactly one deref when the parent captured by value while the child captured by reference, although `UniqueImmBorrow`/`MutBorrow` can insert an additional reborrow. The incorrect result is not merely the absence of the new remapping table: it is a by-move body whose `CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL` field projection refers to the wrong parent upvar and/or drops projections needed to reach the precise child capture.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust async coroutine-closures (async closures) compiled under edition 2021 (and comparisons with edition 2018), especially call-through-`FnOnce`/`AsyncFnOnce` paths that generate the ByMove shim. Inputs include closures that precisely capture struct fields by value or by mutable reference, closures capturing multiple `&mut` variables whose projection paths overlap in shape, `async move ||` closures capturing a mutable reference (implicit reborrow), and revision modes that call the closure normally, call it as `async FnOnce`, or force inference to `FnOnce`.
analysis.trigger: When the ByMoveBody pass constructs the by-move body for a coroutine-closure whose inner coroutine's capture set does not line up one-to-one with the outer coroutine-closure's capture set because of edition-2021 precise closure capture rules (differing capture count and/or additional projections on a captured upvar).
preconditions: The language feature async closures is enabled and an async coroutine-closure is being monomorphized or used as FnOnce/AsyncFnOnce, requiring the ByMove shim.
Edition 2021 precise capture rules are active so the inner coroutine may split a parent capture into multiple captures.
The closure captures fields of a struct or references, allowing additional Field/Deref projections beyond the parent capture's projections.
The outer closure may capture by value while the inner coroutine captures the same upvar by reference, requiring a deref to be peeled in the by-move body.
For the FnOnce kind, the pass checks that every parent capture got remapped and returns early before building the by-move body.
pitfalls: Do not assume equal numbers of parent and child captures: one parent capture may refine into several child captures.

Do not match captures by projection kinds alone; two distinct upvars can have the same projection shape. Also compare the upvar base HIR id (`parent_base.var_path.hir_id == child_base.var_path.hir_id`).
Do not assume the child projection has exactly one deref when peeling a by-ref child capture of a by-value parent capture; implicit reborrows from `UniqueImmBorrow`/`MutBorrow` can add more derefs.
Child field indices must be renumbered to the corresponding parent fields, and the remapped parent capture type must be used for the field projection.
Extra precise-capture projections from the child must be re-applied after the remapped parent field so the rest of the body sees the same place.
A parent capture that does not match the current child must be skipped; bookkeeping should ensure every parent capture is used at least once and none are left over.
For FnOnce, a by-value parent capture borrowed by the child would lead to a borrowck error; the pass asserts this combination does not arise.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `run-pass` UI tests with `check-run-results` and output assertions, under edition 2021, exercising the ByMove shim via multiple revisions: normal call, call as `async FnOnce`, and forced `FnOnce` inference. Cover precise capture of individual struct fields (including mutating one field while leaving another uncaptured), `&mut` structs, `async move` closures, consuming a field, and drop-order/print output. Add an overlapping-projection case with two `&mut` variables to ensure base upvar identity is checked, and a mutable-reference reborrow test with both edition 2018 and 2021 revisions. The expected stdout files demonstrate the semantic results (e.g. the captured field becomes "fixed", the uncaptured field stays unchanged or "uncaptured", and the reborrow test asserts the value increments to 1).
